_comment: ANCHOR SELECTION over the relational target (BACKLOG_LOOP sec2.5-2b, R1/R4 motion). Each pair holds a 2x2 mover (colour 3), an anchor BAR of size 3 (colour 2) and a single-pixel DISTRACTOR (colour 4), all at varying positions; the mover relocates so its bbox top-left lands ON the anchor bar's bbox top-left, dropping the rest (output = the mover alone). Authored to FAIL iter22's to_anchor, which is hard-gated to 'the single other object': there are now TWO other objects, so naming the anchor requires a SELECTOR over the others (here the anchor is the LARGEST other; the distractor is the smallest). The mover is itself the size extreme among all objects (largest) so the existing selector names which object moves; the new content is the anchor SELECTION inside the relational target. Targets vary across pairs (dsts not constant, deltas not constant, never a grid corner) so only to_anchor explains every pair. Solved the intended way it merges into the one value-agnostic object_motion rule (covers +1) with no new detector and no new transformation primitive.
